text:
Marcus Lin: post-game-day debrief thread (kms failure-mode). quick recap while it’s fresh.

What we ran:
- staging + canary tenant (private-ish config)
- injected: KMS throttling (429), timeouts, and one AccessDenied flip (policy deny)

What actually failed:
- decrypt failure rate spiked for ~6 min in canary when we did *timeout + throttling* together.
- a few requests got stuck in retry loop long enough to trip app-level request deadlines (so user saw 5xx even though cache had some coverage)
- dual-read window behaved, but fallback to old key + retries increased tail latency a lot.

What alerts fired / didn’t:
- Fired: `kms_client_error_rate` (good), `kms_circuit_breaker_open` (good), `p99_request_latency` for inference route (late)
- Did NOT fire: per-tenant impact alert (we only saw it in logs), and no page for sustained 401/AccessDenied spikes (we only had a generic “kms errors” bucket)

Action items: please drop concrete fixes + owners below. We should update runbook + alerting doc this week.

Sean Gallagher: +1. timeline from SRE side:
- 10:07 breaker opened (timeouts), recovered around 10:11
- 10:12 when we added throttling, breaker flapped (open/half-open) for ~2 mins
- user-visible errors were mostly 10:12-10:13 because retries pushed us past upstream timeouts

Rafael Mendes: biggest surprise for me: we expected cache to mask most decrypts, but because it was the *data key unwrap* path for a hot shard restart, cache was cold.

Allison Grant: re alerts: our dashboard panel shows it, but no alert on it yet. We have a metric `kms_decrypt_failures_total{tenant=...}` but it’s not in alert rules (and we aggressively cardinality-capped alerts a while ago).

Kevin Osei: AccessDenied case: the error code was clean (`AccessDeniedException` AWS KMS) but our alert rule aggregates all non-2xx as “kms_error”. would be nice to split by `error_code` so we can page Security only on deny/disabled-key vs transient throttle.

Emily Zhao: on the retry loop: current policy is 6 attempts with exponential backoff + jitter, but we’re not respecting the request deadline early enough.
I can add “deadline-aware retries” (stop retrying if <X ms remaining) so we fail fast + fall back (or serve degraded) instead of burning the full budget.

Benji Okafor: question: are we comfortable having fallback continue while breaker is open? right now we still attempt the *secondary key decrypt* even if breaker is open for primary, so we do extra KMS calls under failure.

Sean Gallagher: yeah that’s part of the flapping. breaker open -> we still try old key -> that also hits same KMS -> more pressure.

Hanae Suzuki: for Private specifically, customers often use regional KMS endpoints + SCPs. if they misconfigure policy during rotation, it’s *AccessDenied* and will persist. we should treat that differently than a transient brownout.

Marcus Lin: agree. action items I’m hearing:
1) differentiate deny/disabled vs transient, and route alerts + runbook paths accordingly.
2) deadline-aware retries.
3) breaker behavior with dual-read.

Allison Grant: I’ll own alerting changes. proposal:
- new alert: `kms_access_denied_rate` > 0.5% for 5m (page sec-oncall + sre)
- new alert: `kms_disabled_key_errors` any sustained > 0 for 2m (page)
- adjust existing `kms_error_rate` to ticket-only unless it correlates with `inference_5xx_rate`.
Also add a “tenant top offenders” panel (topN by failures) so oncall can see impact quickly.

Rafael Mendes: + runbook update needed: when breaker is flapping, first step should be “check cache hit ratio + cold start events” not just “increase cache TTL”. increasing TTL didn’t help when cache was empty.

Kevin Osei: for audit: we should ensure we emit audit event on AccessDenied + include key id + tenant id. I saw logs but not sure we’re emitting the structured audit event consistently in the deny path.

incident-bot: Reminder: If this is an incident follow-up, capture: start/end time, customer impact, suspected root cause, mitigations, and links to dashboards/runbooks. Use `/incident create` if needed.

Marcus Lin: not a customer incident (controlled game day), but we should treat it like one. Connor can we add this to release checklist / follow-ups?

Connor O'Brien: yep. I’ll open follow-up tasks under ENG-4258 and add a release checklist item: “kms game day findings resolved/accepted” before flag goes wider.

Benji Okafor: code-side: we can change selection order during dual-read:
- if breaker open, do NOT attempt any KMS calls; only serve from cache; otherwise fail with explicit “kms unavailable” error code.
- if breaker half-open, only allow *one* attempt (new key only), no old-key fallback.
Would reduce load during outage but might increase decrypt failures during rotation window.

Sean Gallagher: from reliability POV I’d rather have predictable fail-fast than retry storms. if we need rotation availability, we can widen the dual-read window but keep it bounded by strict retry limits.

Emily Zhao: +1. I can implement: (a) cap total kms attempts per request to 2 (new then old) and (b) stop all kms attempts if breaker open.
We’ll need a config flag per environment.

Hanae Suzuki: please make sure the error message in Private is actionable (which key, which region, which principal). but sanitized enough for logs.

Kevin Osei: also worth adding explicit guidance to Private rotation doc: “do NOT remove decrypt perms from old key until re-encryption complete + validation check passes.” I still see customers do that.

Allison Grant: did we have an alert for breaker flapping? we only alert on “open” state sustained. flapping is what caused pain.

Sean Gallagher: good call. maybe alert on `breaker_state_transitions_total` rate? if transitions > N/min, it’s basically unstable.

Allison Grant: I’ll add: `kms_breaker_transition_rate` > 10/min for 5m -> page SRE (not Security).

Marcus Lin: can someone drop the exact grafana panel we used? want it in runbook.

Sean Gallagher: this one (internal): https://grafana.prod.redwood/llm-infra/kms?view=game-day (panel IDs 3,7,12 were most useful). I’ll add screenshots to the runbook page.

Rafael Mendes: acceptance criteria update for next game day:
- no more than 0.1% user-visible 5xx during injected throttle/timeout
- breaker open should reduce KMS QPS by >80% within 30s
- alert should identify top impacted tenant within 2 mins

Kevin Osei: + audit event coverage: ensure `kms.decrypt.denied` and `kms.decrypt.disabled_key` emitted with `tenant_id`, `kms_provider`, `key_arn` (hashed ok), `error_code`, `request_id`.

Marcus Lin: locking action items + owners:
- Allison: alert rules + dashboard tweaks (deny/disabled + flapping + tenant topN)
- Emily + Benji: deadline-aware retries + breaker/dual-read behavior changes behind flag
- Sean + Rafael: runbook updates (cache cold-start, breaker flapping, mitigations order) + add grafana links
- Kevin + Hanae: audit event coverage check + doc guidance for Private key policy/rotation sequencing
- Connor: track in rollout checklist + link in ENG-4258

If anyone disagrees with “no KMS calls when breaker open”, speak now. otherwise we’ll treat as default.

Sean Gallagher: +1 default. :thumbsup:

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: will send PR to alert rules today.

Emily Zhao: :thumbsup: I’ll start with retry/deadline logic; will post a diff for review.

Hanae Suzuki: :thumbsup: pls also add a one-liner to the installer preflight output: “KMS perms verified for both encrypt+decrypt on key versions used in rotation”. customers ask for this.

Marcus Lin: noted. thanks all. let’s aim to have runbook + alerting merged before next scheduled game day.
